name: OpenAI Codex

surfaces.label: ChatGPT desktop app (Codex). The agent is the bundled `codex app-server` child, not the Electron host.
OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex extension (VS Code, Cursor). Runs its bundled `codex -c features.code_mode_host=true app-server --analytics-default-enabled` (argv read from the extension's out/extension.js).
Any other `codex app-server`: the shared local daemon (`codex app-server [--remote-control] --listen unix://`) or a third-party stdio client. Hosts many threads.

codex exec (headless terminal run, also what the TypeScript SDK spawns as `codex exec --experimental-json [resume <id>]`). `codex e` and `codex review` are not matched by this surface; review has its own surface below.

codex review: headless code-review turn (`codex review --help`: 'Run a code review non-interactively'). Separate surface because args_contain is AND-only and the interactive TUI surface excludes the word `review`.
codex in a terminal (interactive TUI, also `codex resume` / `codex fork` / `codex agents`)
Codex cloud tasks (chatgpt.com/codex, `codex cloud`). No local process; runs in OpenAI's sandbox.

working_signals.name: Codex is running an active turn
working_signals.meaning: IOPMAssertion PreventUserIdleSystemSleep held in-process (no caffeinate child) for exactly the length of a turn, but ONLY when features.prevent_idle_sleep=true. That flag is experimental and off by default (off on this Mac), so treat presence as proof of working and absence as no information.

working_signals.name: rollout tail has an open turn
working_signals.meaning: Precise form: the newest turn-lifecycle record in the rollout is event_msg/task_started with no later task_complete or turn_aborted, AND the file was written recently. Measured in-turn gaps between records: p50 0.1s, p90 14.5s, p99 56.8s, max 528s (long tool call), so a 30s window misses 4.2% of gaps (72 of 1732) and a 20s window 7.3% (127 of 1732); one 16-turn session only; a bare open turn with a quiet file is either a long tool call, a permission prompt, or a crashed process.

Summed CPU of the process that HOSTS the thread. For a TUI attached to the shared daemon, or the desktop app, that is the `codex app-server` process (one process, many threads), so CPU cannot say which thread is working.

waiting_signals.meaning: Runs when Codex is about to ask for approval (shell escalation, apply_patch, MCP tool, managed-network). Does not run for commands that need no approval. There is no Notification-style hook, and no hook for request_user_input questions.

status {type: active, activeFlags: [waitingOnApproval | waitingOnUserInput]} from a client connected to the app-server (stdio, or unix socket ~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock inferred from strings in the binary). The only source that also covers request_user_input.

waiting_signals.config: tui.notifications (event types agent-turn-complete, approval-requested), tui.notification_method auto|osc9|bel, tui.notification_condition unfocused|always
waiting_signals.meaning: Terminal escape sequence or bell only. Nothing a process outside the terminal can read.

Approval requests, request_user_input and elicitations are NOT persisted to the rollout (rollout/src/policy.rs lists them as not persisted), so a waiting agent looks like a quiet open turn in the transcript.

hooks.config: ~/.codex/hooks.json or [hooks] tables in ~/.codex/config.toml; <repo>/.codex/hooks.json or config.toml (trusted projects only); plugin hooks/hooks.json; managed requirements.toml. New or changed non-managed hooks are skipped until reviewed and trusted in the CLI /hooks screen. Separate legacy `notify = [argv...]` in config.toml fires only for agent-turn-complete and is a single command (already taken on this Mac by the desktop app's Computer Use plugin).

telemetry.how: Off by default. Set [otel] in ~/.codex/config.toml (user level only; ignored in project .codex/config.toml): exporter = { otlp-http = {...} } or { otlp-grpc = {...} } for log events (codex.conversation_starts, codex.api_request, codex.sse_event, codex.user_prompt, codex.tool_decision, codex.tool_result), trace_exporter for traces, metrics_exporter for metrics (turn.e2e_duration_ms, tool.call, approval.requested, hooks.run, thread.started). log_user_prompt=false redacts prompts. Separately, anonymous usage metrics go to OpenAI by default unless [analytics] enabled=false.

sources.claim: A process can be mapped to its thread through an flock on ~/.codex/thread-writer-locks/<thread-id>.lock (lsof shows the holder pid). Holding the lock means the process owns the thread, not that a turn is running.
sources.evidence: https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/rollout/src/writer_lock.rs: WRITER_LOCK_DIR = "thread-writer-locks", path = directory.join(format!("{thread_id}.lock")), file.try_lock() with WouldBlock => 'thread already has an active writer'; stale locks are removed when try_lock succeeds. Locally only .coordination.lock exists (nothing running); the per-thread lock-and-lsof path itself was NOT exercised.

sources.claim: Release tarballs contain a binary named codex-aarch64-apple-darwin, so Homebrew/manual installs may run under that name
sources.evidence: https://api.github.com/repos/openai/codex/releases/latest (rust-v0.159.0) asset names codex-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz/.dmg. The inner binary name and Homebrew's symlink behaviour were not verified: inferred. Upstream README (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/main/README.md line 64): 'Each archive contains a single entry with the platform baked into the name (e.g., codex-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl), so you likely want to rename it to codex after extracting it.' The npm vendor binary and the TS SDK resolver (sdk/typescript/src/exec.ts) use the name `codex`. Release also ships a separate codex-app-server-aarch64-apple-darwin asset; whether a process runs under that name is unknown.

sources.claim: Process rules classify the expected argv shapes (synthetic test, not a live process)

notes: Not verified-locally: no Codex process was running, so the probe never classified a live instance. The agent loop lives in `codex app-server` (desktop app asar and IDE extension JS both spawn it; the TUI embeds one or attaches to the shared daemon, per app-server-daemon/README.md), so 'one process = one session' is false: one app-server hosts many threads and its CPU and children cannot be attributed to a thread. Best per-thread working check: newest rollout record is task_started (no task_complete/turn_aborted) AND the file grew in the last ~30s AND ~/.codex/thread-writer-locks/<thread>.lock is held by a live pid (lsof). Read thread_history_1.sqlite with mode=ro (not immutable=1) if used live. tool_children is deliberately absent: MCP servers (node_repl etc.) are long-lived children of the host and would read as work; unverified without a live process. Session-id flag mapping only works for `codex resume <id>` / `codex fork <id>`; a fresh TUI session carries no id in argv, use the writer lock. Executable names seen: `codex` (standalone, SDK, extension, desktop-bundled). $CODEX_HOME relocates everything above. Known gaps: the `codex e` alias matches no surface (a bare `e` cannot be expressed: args_contain is AND-only and substring-based); `codex review` is handled by its own surface; because exclude_args is matched against whitespace-split argv words, a TUI started with a prompt containing an excluded word (`codex fix the update logic`) is missed, and args_contain is a substring test so a prompt mentioning `app-server` or `exec` can land on the wrong surface (same kind, so harmless); path_contains is a prefix match on argv[0], so any binary under ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex* (e.g. codex-code-mode-host, codex_chronicle) would match if it ever received an `app-server` argument; `codex agents` (a session browser attached to the daemon, `codex agents --help`) is counted as a TUI session, unverified whether it should be; a different product with a binary simply named `codex` would match the TUI surface, since names carry no path check; the release asset codex-app-server-aarch64-apple-darwin is not in names (unknown whether it is ever run); the npm wrapper `node .../codex.js` is not matched on purpose (its child, the vendor `codex`, is). Live run 2026-10-01: the exec surface was matched (reported as tui, since the exec surface scored no higher); the writer lock is the precise signal and needs a lock_file signal kind to be evaluated; CPU alone flickers within one turn.
